questions.question: A developer needs to set up an SSL security certificate for a client's eCommerce website in order to use the HTTPS protocol. Which of the following AWS services can be used to deploy the required SSL server certificates? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: To deploy SSL/TLS server certificates, you use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) — the preferred tool — or the AWS IAM certificate store, which is used for resources in Regions ACM does not support. Route 53 is DNS only and does not deploy certificates, so it is not a correct choice here.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services scale automatically without your intervention? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 (B) and AWS Lambda (C) scale automatically with no user intervention. EC2, EMR, and EBS require you to provision or adjust capacity.

questions.question: A company is planning to migrate an application from Amazon EC2 to AWS Lambda to use a serverless architecture. Which of the following will be the responsibility of AWS after migration? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: After moving to Lambda (serverless), AWS handles capacity management (B) and operating-system maintenance (D). The customer still owns application code/logic, access control, and data.

questions.question: How do ELBs improve the reliability of your application?

options.text: By distributing traffic across multiple S3 buckets.
By replicating data to multiple availability zones.
By ensuring that only healthy targets receive traffic.

questions.explanation: An Elastic Load Balancer improves reliability by performing health checks and routing traffic only to healthy targets. It does not balance across S3 buckets, replicate data, or create read replicas.

questions.question: A company needs to migrate their website from on-premises to AWS. Security is a major concern for them, so they need to host their website on hardware that is NOT shared with other AWS customers. Which of the following EC2 instance options meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: Dedicated Instances run on hardware not shared with other AWS customers, satisfying the single-tenancy requirement. On-Demand, Spot, and Reserved are pricing models that (by default) run on shared hardware.

questions.question: A customer is planning to move billions of images and videos to be stored on Amazon S3. The customer has approximately 60 Petabytes of data to move. Which of the following AWS Services is the best choice to transfer the data to AWS?
questions.explanation: AWS Snowmobile moves exabyte-scale data; 60 PB is best handled by Snowmobile rather than many Snowball devices or network-based S3 Transfer Acceleration. A VPC is networking, not data transfer.

questions.question: A company plans to migrate a large amount of archived data to AWS. The archived data must be maintained for a period of 5 years and must be retrievable within 5 hours of a request. What is the most cost-effective AWS storage service to use?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Glacier (Flexible Retrieval) is the most cost-effective option for long-term archives that must be retrievable within hours (standard retrieval is typically 3–5 hours), meeting the 5-hour requirement. EFS, S3 Standard, and EBS cost more for cold archival data.

questions.question: Which AWS Service is used to manage user permissions?
questions.explanation: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) manages user permissions across AWS. Security Groups filter network traffic, ECS runs containers, and Support is a help service.

questions.question: Which support plan includes AWS Support Concierge Service?
questions.explanation: The AWS Support Concierge Service is included with the Enterprise Support plan. Business and Developer plans do not include the Concierge, and 'Premium'/'Standard' are not AWS support tier names.

questions.question: A company needs to track resource changes using the API call history. Which AWS service can help the company achieve this goal?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records the API call history, letting you track who changed which resource and when. Config tracks configuration state, CloudWatch monitors metrics, and CloudFormation provisions infrastructure.

questions.question: What are the benefits of using an AWS-managed service? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Provides complete control over the virtual infrastructure.
Allows customers to deliver new solutions faster.
Eliminates the need to encrypt data.
Allows developers to control all patching related activities.

questions.explanation: AWS-managed services let customers deliver solutions faster (B) and lower operational complexity (C) by offloading undifferentiated heavy lifting. They do not give full infrastructure control, remove the need to encrypt data, or hand patching to the customer.

questions.question: Which of the following are use cases for Amazon S3? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Hosting websites that require sustained high CPU utilization.
A media store for the CloudFront service.
Processing data streams at any scale.

questions.explanation: Amazon S3 use cases include hosting static websites (A) and serving as a media/origin store for CloudFront (D). It is not for sustained high-CPU workloads, relational databases, or stream processing.

questions.question: What is the AWS’ recommendation regarding access keys?

options.text: Delete all access keys and use passwords instead.
Only share them with trusted people.
Save them within your application code.

questions.explanation: AWS recommends rotating access keys regularly to limit exposure if a key is compromised. You should never embed keys in code or share them.

questions.question: What is the AWS IAM feature that provides an additional layer of security on top of user-name and password authentication?
questions.explanation: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds an extra layer on top of username/password sign-in. Key pairs and access keys are credentials, and an SDK is a development tool.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using an API to access AWS Services?

options.text: It improves the performance of AWS resources.
It reduces the time needed to provision AWS resources.
It reduces the number of developers necessary.
It allows for programmatic management of AWS resources.

questions.explanation: APIs allow programmatic management of AWS resources, enabling automation and integration. They do not inherently improve performance, provision faster on their own, or reduce headcount.

questions.question: A company is planning to migrate a database with high read/write activity to AWS. What is the best storage option to use?
questions.explanation: Amazon EBS provides low-latency block storage suited to a database with high read/write activity. S3 is object storage, Glacier is archival, and Storage Gateway is hybrid.

questions.question: How can AWS customers track and avoid over-spending on underutilized reserved instances?

options.text: Customers can add all AWS accounts to an AWS Organization, enable Consolidated Billing, and turn off Reserved Instance sharing.
Customers can use Amazon Neptune to track and analyze their usage patterns, detect underutilized reserved instances, and then sell them on the Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance Marketplace.
Customers can use the AWS Budgets service to track the reserved instances usage and set up alert notifications when their utilization drops below the threshold that they define.
Customers can use Amazon CloudTrail to automatically check for unused reservations and get recommendations to reduce their bill.

questions.explanation: AWS Budgets can track Reserved Instance utilization and send alerts when it drops below a defined threshold, helping avoid paying for unused reservations. Neptune, CloudTrail, and the marketplace path described do not provide this tracking/alerting.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that provides five times the performance of a standard MySQL database?
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora delivers up to five times the throughput of standard MySQL while remaining MySQL-compatible. Redshift, DynamoDB, and Neptune are not MySQL replacements.

questions.question: What does AWS Service Catalog provide?

options.text: It enables customers to quickly find descriptions and use cases for AWS services.
It enables customers to explore the different catalogs of AWS services.
It simplifies organizing and governing commonly deployed IT services.
It allows developers to deploy infrastructure on AWS using familiar programming languages.

questions.explanation: AWS Service Catalog lets organizations create and manage approved catalogs of IT services, simplifying governance and standardized deployment. It is not a service descriptions directory or an IaC programming tool.

questions.question: For managed services like Amazon DynamoDB, which of the below is AWS responsible for? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: For a managed service like DynamoDB, AWS is responsible for patching the database software (C) and operating-system maintenance (D). The customer manages credentials, access policies, and access logging.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS Services helps with planning application migration to the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: AWS Application Discovery Service collects information about on-premises servers and dependencies to help plan a migration. Migration Hub tracks progress, and DMS migrates databases.

questions.question: A company is trying to analyze the costs applied to their AWS account recently. Which of the following provides them the most granular data about their AWS costs and usage?
questions.explanation: The AWS Cost & Usage Report (CUR) provides the most granular, line-item detail of AWS costs and usage. Cost Explorer offers higher-level visualization, and CloudWatch is for metrics.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the concept of an AWS region?

options.text: An AWS Region is a geographical location with a collection of Edge locations.
An AWS Region is a virtual network dedicated only to a single AWS customer.
An AWS Region is a geographical location with a collection of Availability Zones.
An AWS Region represents the country where the AWS infrastructure exist.

questions.explanation: An AWS Region is a geographic location containing a collection of isolated Availability Zones. It is not a per-customer network, a single country marker, or a set of Edge Locations.

questions.question: A company has discovered that multiple S3 buckets were deleted, but it is unclear who deleted the buckets. Which of the following can the company use to determine the identity that deleted the buckets?
questions.explanation: CloudTrail logs capture the identity, time, and source of API actions such as deleting an S3 bucket, revealing who deleted it. SNS, SQS, and CloudWatch logs do not record this identity information.

questions.question: Which of the following are factors in determining the appropriate database technology to use for a specific workload? (Choose TWO)

options.text: The number of reads and writes per second.

questions.explanation: Choosing a database technology depends on the read/write throughput required (C) and the nature of the queries (D). Availability Zones, data sovereignty, and software bugs are not the primary technology-selection factors here.

questions.question: What are the benefits of implementing a tagging strategy for AWS resources? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Quickly identify resources that belong to a specific project.
Quickly identify software solutions on AWS.
Track API calls in your AWS account.
Quickly identify deleted resources and their metadata.
Track AWS spending across multiple resources.

questions.explanation: Tagging helps you quickly identify resources belonging to a project (A) and track AWS spending across resources via cost allocation tags (E). Tags do not catalog software, track API calls, or recover deleted resources.

questions.question: What are AWS shared controls?

options.text: Controls that are solely the responsibility of the customer based on the application they are deploying within AWS services.
Controls that a customer inherits from AWS.
Controls that apply to both the infrastructure layer and customer layers.
Controls that the customer and AWS collaborate together upon to secure the infrastructure.

questions.explanation: AWS shared controls are controls that apply to both the infrastructure layer and the customer layers, but in separate contexts (e.g., patch management, configuration management, awareness & training). They are not solely customer-owned, fully inherited from AWS, nor a literal collaboration on securing the infrastructure.

questions.question: Which design principles relate to performance efficiency in AWS? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Build multi-region architectures to better serve global customers.
Implement strong Identity and Access controls.

questions.explanation: Performance Efficiency design principles include using multi-Region architectures to serve global customers (A) and adopting serverless architectures (D). Applying security at all layers, strong IAM, and audit logging belong to the Security pillar.

questions.question: Which of the below are responsibilities of the customer when using Amazon EC2? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Setup and operation of managed databases.

questions.explanation: When using EC2, customers are responsible for protecting their sensitive data (A) and installing/configuring third-party software (E). AWS patches the underlying infrastructure and maintains hardware; managed databases are a separate service.

questions.question: Why would an organization decide to use AWS over an on-premises data center? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Organizations choose AWS for elastic resources that scale with demand (C) and for cost savings (E). AWS does not give free commercial licenses, free technical support to all, or on-site customer audits.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services can help you perform security analysis and regulatory compliance auditing? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector (A) performs automated security assessments and AWS Config (E) evaluates resource configurations for compliance; both support security analysis and compliance auditing. Virtual Private Gateway, Batch, and ECS do not.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)?

options.text: Amazon EC2 is considered a Serverless Web Service.
Amazon EC2 eliminates the need to invest in hardware upfront.
Amazon EC2 can launch as many or as few virtual servers as needed.

questions.explanation: The false statement is that EC2 is a 'serverless' web service — EC2 provides virtual servers you manage, so it is not serverless. The other statements (no upfront hardware, elastic count, scalable computing) are all true.

questions.question: What is the AWS Compute service that executes code only when triggered by events?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda runs your code only in response to events (triggers), with no servers to manage. CloudWatch monitors, Transit Gateway connects networks, and EC2 runs continuously.

questions.question: Both AWS and traditional IT distributors provide a wide range of virtual servers to meet their customers’ requirements. What is the name of these virtual servers in AWS?
questions.explanation: In AWS, the virtual servers are called Amazon EC2 instances. EBS snapshots are volume backups, VPC is networking, and 'Managed Servers' is not an AWS product.

questions.question: What is the framework created by AWS Professional Services that helps organizations design a road map to successful cloud adoption?
questions.explanation: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) helps organizations build a roadmap for successful cloud adoption across perspectives like business, people, governance, platform, security, and operations. Secrets Manager, WAF, and EFS are unrelated to adoption planning.

questions.question: TYMO Cloud Corp is looking forward to migrating their entire on-premises data center to AWS. What tool can they use to perform a cost-benefit analysis of moving to the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: The AWS TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) Calculator was AWS's tool for comparing the cost of running workloads on-premises versus AWS. Note: AWS has since retired the standalone TCO Calculator and folded cost comparison into the AWS Pricing Calculator, so in current practice you would use the Pricing Calculator — but for this question's intent, the TCO Calculator is the cost-benefit comparison tool.

questions.question: Which of the following activities supports the Operational Excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.text: Using AWS Trusted Advisor to find underutilized resources.
Using AWS CloudTrail to record user activities.
Using AWS CloudFormation to manage infrastructure as code.
Deploying an application in multiple Availability Zones.

questions.explanation: Using AWS CloudFormation to manage infrastructure as code supports the Operational Excellence pillar by making operations repeatable, automated, and version-controlled. Trusted Advisor (cost/perf), CloudTrail (security/audit), and multi-AZ deployment (reliability) map to other pillars.

questions.question: Why do many startup companies prefer AWS over traditional on-premises solutions? (Choose TWO)

options.text: AWS allows them to pay later when their business succeed.
AWS can build complete data centers faster than any other Cloud provider.
Using AWS, they can reduce time-to-market by focusing on business activities rather than on building and managing data centers.
AWS removes the need to invest in operational expenditure.
Using AWS allows companies to replace large capital expenditure with low variable costs.

questions.explanation: Startups prefer AWS to reduce time-to-market by focusing on their business rather than building data centers (C), and to replace large capital expenditure with low variable costs (E). AWS does not let you defer all payment until success or remove all operating expense.

questions.question: What are the benefits of using DynamoDB? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Automatically scales to meet required throughput capacity.
Provides resizable instances to match the current demand.
Supports both relational and non-relational data models.
Supports the most popular NoSQL database engines such as CouchDB and MongoDB.

questions.explanation: DynamoDB automatically scales to meet throughput demand (A) and offers single-digit millisecond latency (D). It is purely NoSQL (not relational), does not provide 'instances,' and uses its own engine rather than CouchDB/MongoDB.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to protect data at rest on Amazon S3? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: To protect data at rest on S3 from the listed options, use Versioning (A) to guard against accidental overwrite/deletion and Permissions (C) to control access. Deduplication, decryption, and conversion are not S3 data-protection features.

questions.question: As part of the AWS Migration Acceleration Program (MAP), what does AWS provide to accelerate Enterprise adoption of AWS? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: The AWS Migration Acceleration Program (MAP) provides access to AWS Partners (A) and AWS Professional Services (C) to accelerate enterprise migrations. Artifact, Athena, and Pinpoint are not MAP migration resources.

questions.question: AWS recommends some practices to help organizations avoid unexpected charges on their bill. Which of the following is NOT one of these practices?

options.text: Deleting unused EBS volumes after terminating an EC2instance.
Releasing unused Elastic IPs after terminating an EC2instance.

questions.explanation: Deleting an unused Auto Scaling launch configuration does NOT save money because launch configurations are free. Unused EBS volumes, Elastic Load Balancers, and unattached Elastic IPs do incur charges, so deleting/releasing them avoids cost.

questions.question: What is the AWS tool that can help a company visualize their AWS spending in the last few months?
questions.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes spending trends over recent months with graphs and filters. The Pricing Calculator estimates future cost, Budgets sets thresholds, and Consolidated Billing aggregates accounts.

questions.question: When running a workload in AWS, the customer is NOT responsible for: (Select TWO)
questions.explanation: Customers are NOT responsible for data center operations (C) or the security of the underlying infrastructure (E) — those are AWS's responsibility. Customers do run their own pen tests, reserve capacity, and meet their compliance obligations.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to send promotional text messages (SMS) to more than 200 countries worldwide?
questions.explanation: Amazon SNS (Simple Notification Service) can send SMS text messages to recipients in more than 200 countries. SES sends email, S3 stores objects, and SQS is a queue.

questions.question: Which of the following allows you to create new RDS instances? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: You can create new RDS instances with AWS CloudFormation (C) (infrastructure as code) and the AWS Management Console (E). CodeDeploy deploys app code, Quick Starts are reference architectures, and DMS migrates data.

questions.question: One of the major advantages of using AWS is cost savings. What does AWS provide to reduce the cost of running Amazon EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: Per-second billing reduces EC2 costs by charging only for the exact seconds used (Linux, one-minute minimum) instead of rounding up to the hour. There are no instance start-up fees or paid tagging.

questions.question: Which AWS Group assists customers in achieving their desired business outcomes?
questions.explanation: AWS Professional Services is the consulting team that helps customers achieve their desired business outcomes on AWS. Trusted Advisor is automated checks, and the Security Team/Concierge serve other roles.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature is used to manage the keys used to encrypt customer data?
questions.explanation: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) creates and manages the encryption keys used to protect customer data. SCPs restrict account actions, MFA is authentication, and Macie discovers sensitive data.

questions.question: Which AWS Service allows customers to download AWS SOC & PCI reports?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for downloading AWS compliance reports such as SOC and PCI. The Well-Architected Tool reviews workloads, Glue is ETL, and Chime is communications.
